title: Achuar - Wikipedia
text: The Achuar are an indigenous people of the Americas belonging to the Jivaroan family, alongside the Shuar, Shiwiar, Awajun, and Wampis.

title: Achuar Language and the Achuar Indian Tribe (Ashuar, Shiwiar...)
text: Like other Jivaroan languages, Achuar is an agglutinative language with SOV word order. It is spoken by 7000 people in the Achuar and Shiwiar tribes of Peru and Ecuador today. Thanks for your interest in indigenous American languages!

title: Achuar-Shiwiar | Ethnologue Free
text: Achuar-Shiwiar is a stable indigenous language of Ecuador and Peru. It belongs to the Jivaroan language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Achuar-Shiwiar Language, Etymology, History, Grammar, Phonology...
text: Achuar-Shiwiar, also known simply as Achuar, is a member of the Jivaroan language family. The Jivaroan family includes several closely related languages spoken in the upper Amazon region of South America, primarily in Ecuador and Peru.

title: Achuar (Achuar Chicham) — 20 words & pronunciations | Word Map
text: Achuar (Achuar Chicham, "Achuar speech"; also Achuar-Shiwiar) is a Jivaroan language spoken in the Marañón–Pastaza ecotone of the Peru-Ecuador border.

title: Achuar-Shiwiar profile. Information about Achuar-Shiwiar.
text: Achuar-Shiwiar is an American Jivaroan language spoken along the Morona, Macusari, Tigre, Huasaga, and Corrientes rivers in Peru and along the Pastaza and Bobonaza rivers in Ecuador. The language is also known as Achuar, Achual, Achuara, Achuale, Jivaro, and Maina.
